Sample learning experience · 5–7 minutes · Framework Levels 1–2 (Foundations & Productivity)

AI for Public Service Productivity: Responsible Use in Everyday Work

This is an illustrative demonstration. The organisation, people and documents are fictional, and the data is synthetic. Nothing you enter is stored or sent anywhere. It is a scripted simulation and does not use a live AI service.

Step 1 of 6 · Introduction

Learning objectives

By the end of this module, you will be able to:

  1. Classify common work tasks as appropriate, appropriate with safeguards, or not appropriate for an approved AI assistant, based on data sensitivity and accountability.
  2. Identify at least three errors or risks in an AI-generated draft before it is released.
  3. Apply four safeguards to an AI-assisted task: protect personal data, verify, disclose, and keep human sign-off.

Scenario · fictional

You are Jordan Pinder, a Senior Officer in the fictional Department of Licensing Services.

Your department has just been given an approved, organisation-licensed AI assistant. This morning you have 40 public enquiries about the (fictional) Small Business Licence Renewal. Your Director also wants a one-page briefing by 3:00 p.m.

The AI assistant could save you hours, but only if you use it well. Here are five tasks on your list today.

Activity 1 · Should you use AI for this?

Objective 1. For each task on Jordan's list, choose the best option.

Task 1 Summarise the department's publicly published renewal guidelines into a plain-language FAQ.

Task 2 Paste a member of the public's email, which includes their full name, National Insurance number and a medical condition, into a free public chatbot to draft a reply.

Task 3 Ask the AI assistant to decide which applicants should receive a fee waiver.

Task 4 Use the approved assistant to summarise your team's internal meeting notes for the Director's briefing.

Task 5 Use the approved assistant to draft a courteous reply template with placeholders such as [Name] and [Reference No.].

Activity 2 · Review the AI draft

Objective 2. You asked the approved assistant to draft a reply to a business owner whose renewal is late. Review the draft and select every sentence that must be corrected before it is sent.

Sentences in the AI-generated draft

Practical considerations

Privacy

Use only approved tools. Remove names, ID numbers, health details and other personal data unless policy explicitly allows otherwise.

Accuracy

Treat AI output as a first draft. Verify facts, figures, dates and legal references against authoritative sources.

Confidentiality

Keep Cabinet, procurement, personnel and other restricted material out of AI tools unless they are specifically authorised for it.

Human oversight

Decisions about people's rights, benefits or obligations stay with accountable officers. Review before you release anything.

Objective 3 Before you send any AI-assisted work, which of these safeguards apply? Select all that apply.

Knowledge check

Five short questions. Choose the best answer for each one.

Question 1 The approved AI assistant gives you a statistic for your Director's briefing. What should you do first?

Question 2 Which information should never be entered into an AI tool that is not approved?

Question 3 Who is accountable for a letter you send that was drafted with AI?

Question 4 An AI draft cites a regulation you do not recognise. What is the best response?

Question 5 Which combination best describes responsible AI use in everyday public service work?

Your results

Competency is demonstrated at 80% or higher overall, with at least 60% on each objective. This is a demonstration, and no results are saved.

About this design

This module shows the design approach I propose for Framework Levels 1–2. It sets measurable objectives, puts learners in authentic scenarios, and asks them to make decisions rather than recall facts. Each objective is assessed, feedback explains the reasoning, and completion requires demonstrated competency. Seat time alone does not count. In a live programme, the scenarios, policies and approved tools would be replaced with the Ministry's own, following the training needs assessment.
